items.title: CI pipeline that runs the whole gate on every push
items.summary: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml whose primary job runs `make check` on push/PR, plus lint, native-kernel build, and a cross-OS determinism lane; gate CI against the local gate with a meta-test.
items.description: DoR: BL-002 (make check) merged; run_tests.sh green on clean main; uv-sync-vs-pip install path decided; flaky/asset-dependent tests catalogued and skipif-guarded. Spec: jobs test(matrix 3.10-3.12 = make check), determinism-cross-os(macos+windows, non-blocking first), lint(ruff), native-kernels(build audioforge/native/*.c); add tests/test_ci_make_check_sync.py; cache uv + compiled kernels; trigger push+PR to main; README badge.
items.rationale: AudioForge has NO .github/ and no CI: every drift gate, determinism test, and regression fixture passes only when a human runs scripts/run_tests.sh, so the entire contract-discipline investment is advisory. FrameForge's CI primary job IS `make check`, pinned by tests/test_ci_make_check_sync.py so CI can never silently drop a gate.
acceptance_criteria: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists; a PR that drifts docs/ir.schema.json from ir_json_schema() fails CI
`test` job green on main across the 3.10-3.12 matrix
tests/test_ci_make_check_sync.py fails if a target diverges between `make check` and the workflow
green-main CI run URL recorded; README shows a passing CI badge
RELEASE_NOTES.md/CHANGELOG.md records the addition

items.title: Makefile composing every gate into one `make check`

items.description: DoR: BL-004/BL-005 target commands specified (may stub to true, but names fixed now); confirm POSIX make in CI. Spec: targets help/test/schema-check/manifest-check/docs-check/lint/format-check/drift-check/verify-samples/native; each *-check exits non-zero on drift and writes nothing; `check: lint format-check schema-check manifest-check docs-check drift-check test`; add tests/test_makefile_targets.py; `test` target shells out to run_tests.sh (no duplicated suite list).
items.rationale: AudioForge has no Makefile; the only orchestration is scripts/run_tests.sh, a test runner not a composed gate (no schema regen-check, lint, doc-build, manifest-freshness as named targets; no `make help` for agents). FrameForge's `make check` composes twelve gates that developers and CI run identically.

`make help` lists every target with a one-line description
each *-check returns non-zero when its source is drifted (demonstrated for schema-check)

items.title: Golden-audio oracle with a committed hash lockfile
items.summary: Curate a small fast golden .af corpus, commit a tests/golden/audio.lock.json hash lock (no WAVs), and add render_golden.py with --check/--update/--strict that classifies hash mismatches as cosmetic (sub-epsilon) vs real drift.
items.description: DoR: float-reduction-order knobs (BLAS threading, numpy reduction, FFT backend) identified and a pinning strategy chosen; corpus specs render < ~10s total; epsilon defined with a cited rationale (e.g. cosmetic = max-abs < -120 dBFS). Spec: tests/golden/audio/ (5-10 specs across synth/sampler/fx/limiter/convolution/pack/groove); audio.lock.json {spec_hash,output_sha256,sr,channels,frames}; render_golden.py --check (hash then tolerance-classify) / --update / --strict; pin single-thread BLAS + record numeric env; make golden-check + CI strict same-OS + tolerant cross-OS lanes.
items.rationale: AudioForge's only reproducibility oracle is `verify` (re-render vs a manifest that travels with output) and one AST golden; there is no tests/-resident golden-audio corpus or hash lockfile a fresh clone can gate against, and no cosmetic-vs-real-drift distinction (brittle for float audio across environments). This gate is the cross-track pivot: every Track-M item alters render bytes and cannot merge without it.
acceptance_criteria: tests/golden/audio.lock.json committed; WAVs are NOT committed
render_golden.py --check passes on main same-OS and fails on a deliberate coefficient change
cosmetic/real classification exercised by a test injecting a sub-epsilon (pass) and a supra-epsilon (fail) perturbation
--update re-pins reproducibly

items.title: Unify the dual IR source of truth into one typed model
items.summary: Make ir_schema.py DERIVE its JSON-Schema enums from schema.py's registries (Phase A, kills the HIGH duplicate-source coupling) with a sync test; optionally introduce a typed IR model generating the schema (Phase B, ADR-gated).
items.description: DoR: the exact duplicated literals between schema.py and ir_schema.py enumerated from drift-risk-map; explicit Phase-A-only vs Phase-A+B decision recorded as an ADR (Pydantic v2 vs dataclass+TypedDict tradeoff) — MUST NOT start without it; BL-005 merged. Spec Phase A: ir_schema.py imports schema.py registries, delete duplicated literals, add tests/test_schema_sources_sync.py. Phase B (optional): typed model generates docs/ir.schema.json (subsumes BL-005), validate_spec = model validation + semantic rules. Ship Phase A and stop if time-constrained (~70% value at ~20% cost).
items.rationale: Two hand-synced IR sources must agree: schema.py (KINDS/LAYER_TYPES/OSC_SHAPES/FX_TYPES/AUTO_TARGETS + validate_spec) and ir_schema.py (a hand-built JSON-Schema dict + validate_ir_schema). The same facts are encoded twice; the repo's own drift-risk-map rates this HIGH and drift_inspect.py that detects it is unwired (BL-013). This is the largest genuine structural weakness FrameForge's practice would fix. It is the one item where 'the current approach is not broken' is a legitimate stop — do the cheap enforcement wins first.
acceptance_criteria: Phase A: no IR fact (osc shape, fx type, layer type, auto target, kind) stated in more than one module; ir_schema.py derives from schema.py
Phase A: tests/test_schema_sources_sync.py passes and fails if a new osc shape is added to schema.py but not reflected in the generated JSON Schema
Phase A: drift_inspect.py reports the HIGH registry coupling as resolved (and is wired per BL-013)
Phase A: all determinism/contract tests still green (byte-identical renders)
Phase B (if chosen): a single typed model generates docs/ir.schema.json; validate_spec keeps the v2.14 'render-time SpecError pre-reported by validate' property; the Pydantic/dataclass ADR is merged

items.title: Cross-platform numeric-determinism pack
items.summary: Record a numeric-environment descriptor (numpy/scipy/BLAS/FFT/kernel-hashes/CPU-flags) in every render manifest, emit a loud numeric_environment_drift diagnostic on mismatch, pin BLAS threading/FFT during deterministic renders, and extend the golden cross-environment lane to attribute diffs.

Highest-uncertainty item.

items.title: Formal transformation operators + transformation networks
items.summary: Layer the DSL transforms (transpose/invert/retrograde) onto BL-017's Tn/TnI as composable algebraic operators and add a transformation-network evaluator (named operator sequence/graph applied to a motif or chord stream), with grammar/GBNF productions.
items.description: DoR: BL-017 merged (operators to compose); decision on how far toward full Lewinian networks vs a linear operator pipeline (recommend linear pipeline first; graph later only if a use case demands it - no gold-plating). Spec: DSL invert/transpose become pc-set operators applied to events; transformation-network evaluator for a named-operator sequence (T5, I, R, a UTT from BL-019); grammar + GBNF for the operator sequence so an LLM samples only well-formed networks.
items.rationale: DSL play {transform} offers transpose/diatonic/invert/retrograde/stretch as concrete note-event edits, not composable algebraic operators, and there is no transformation network (a labeled graph of operators across a passage). Source: Lewin GMIT (Oxford 2007, ISBN 978-0-19-531713-8); Hook Ch. 9 attested #16.
acceptance_criteria: `play motif {ops: T5 I R}` produces the operator-composed result; a test asserts associativity/round-trips against BL-017's algebra
grammar accepts valid operator sequences and rejects malformed ones (test_grammar_token_sync.py extended)
renders byte-stable under the golden gate

items.title: Neo-Riemannian triadic transformations (P/L/R, UTT) + Tonnetz
items.summary: New audioforge/theory_triads.py: represent a consonant triad as (root_pc, mode), implement neo-Riemannian P/L/R (PLR group order 24) and the general UTT, plus tonnetz_neighbors for shortest-path chromatic progressions; DSL sugar compiling to the existing literal-chord stream.
items.description: DoR: BL-017 (pc-sets) and BL-018 (operator plumbing) merged; triad representation reconciled with theory.parse_chord so P/L/R output round-trips to existing chord symbols. Spec: theory_triads.py (root_pc, mode in {major,minor}) + P/L/R + compositions (PLR group order 24) + general UTT <sign,t+,t-> with composition; tonnetz_neighbors(triad) => P/L/R-adjacent triads (Tonnetz edges) for shortest-path progressions; DSL play <triad> {plr: L R P} and/or `progression via tonnetz from Cmaj to Abmaj` sugar compiling to literal chords.
items.rationale: No P/L/R, no UTT, no Tonnetz anywhere. AudioForge cannot express smooth chromatic third-relations (C major -> E minor by a single L) that are the core of 19th-century and film-score harmony - directly relevant to the orchestral renders/ the project already produces. Source: Hook §1.4 Tonnetz (#8) + Ch. 8 UTT/neo-Riemannian (#15); Hook JMT 46 (2002) DOI 10.1215/00222909-2005-002; Cohn Audacious Euphony (Oxford 2012).
acceptance_criteria: P/L/R verified against their definitions on ALL 24 triads (P(Cmaj)=Cmin, L(Cmaj)=Emin, R(Cmaj)=Amin), exhaustively
the generated PLR group has order 24 (test); UTT composition is associative (test)
a Tonnetz shortest-path progression renders and is byte-stable
AGENTS.md / DSL spec document the new directive
references: Julian Hook, Exploring Musical Spaces (Oxford 2022, ISBN 978-0-19-024601-3, DOI 10.1093/oso/9780190246013.001.0001) §1.4 (#8), Ch. 8 (#15)
Hook, Uniform Triadic Transformations, JMT 46 (2002), DOI 10.1215/00222909-2005-002

items.title: Scale & mode system (modes, pentatonic, octatonic, maximally-even)
items.summary: New audioforge/theory_scales.py: a registry of named collections (7 diatonic modes, harmonic/melodic minor, pentatonic, whole-tone, octatonic, chromatic) each as intervals + pc-set, with a maximally_even(n,c) generator; wire the DSL scale: directive, diatonic_transpose, and the out-of-scale diagnostic to consume it.
items.description: DoR: BL-017 merged (pc-set machinery); the maximally_even generator's output for diatonic (7-in-12) and octatonic (8-in-12) checked against known collections before it is trusted (derive then verify). Spec: theory_scales.py registry + maximally_even(n,c) (Clough-Douthett); wire dsl._scale_pitch_classes + theory.diatonic_transpose + out-of-scale diagnostic to the registry; DSL scale: <name> directive (grammar + GBNF); analyze reports best-fit collection.
items.rationale: dsl.py defines only MAJOR/MINOR interval lists and _scale_pitch_classes handles only those two; theory.diatonic_transpose accepts an arbitrary interval list but no caller ever supplies one other than major/minor. No church modes, pentatonic, harmonic/melodic minor, whole-tone, or octatonic. Source: Hook diatonic dpc(n)/Dorian (#532), pentatonic/whole-tone/octatonic (#364), maximally even Ch. 14 (#6609); Clough-Douthett JMT 35 (1991) DOI 10.2307/843811; Carey-Clampitt MTS 11 (1989) DOI 10.2307/745935 (well-formed NOT attested in corpus).
acceptance_criteria: every registered collection has a test pinning its pcs; maximally_even reproduces the diatonic, pentatonic, and octatonic sets exactly
scale: dorian (and friends) drives diatonic_transpose and the out-of-scale diagnostic; a D-Dorian passage raises no false out-of-scale warnings
renders byte-stable under the golden gate

Carey & Clampitt, Aspects of Well-Formed Scales, MTS 11 (1989), DOI 10.2307/745935

items.title: Tuning & temperament engine (activate the inert tuning: directive)
items.summary: Create audioforge/tuning.py (n-EDO, just intonation, historical temperaments, Scala .scl/.kbm import; cents-exact) and thread it through the ENTIRE pitch->frequency path (dsl.note_to_freq, library.py, plan.py), gated on spec.notation.tuning with a 12-TET default; prove it drives the render via an FFT assertion.
items.description: DoR: BL-006 golden oracle exists (12-TET renders must be provably unchanged); default-path guarantee specified (tuning absent => byte-identical: resolver is a no-op returning 440*2**(x/12)); reference cents for >=1 JI table and 1 historical temperament sourced from Barbour (no hand-invented ratios). Spec: tuning.py resolver pitch->freq for n-EDO/JI/quarter-comma meantone/Werckmeister III/Scala .scl(+.kbm), cents-exact; thread through note_to_freq + library.py resample + plan.py gated on spec.notation.tuning (default 12-TET); interop exports non-12-EDO as pitch-bend/MPE + MusicXML microtonal accidentals (document lossy cases); FFT assertion that a non-12-EDO degree's fundamental lands at the specified cents.
items.rationale: CORRECTNESS DEFECT, not a missing feature: the DSL directive `tuning: edo divisions=N base=A4 hz=440` parses and is stored in spec.notation.tuning, but NO code reads it - every pitch->freq conversion is hardcoded 12-TET (note_to_freq = 440*2**(x/12); library.py/plan.py resample with 2**(st/12)). The engine accepts a microtuning instruction and silently renders 12-TET - an unverified capability claim shipped to users (PALS's LAW). Highest-leverage Track-M item.
acceptance_criteria: a 19-EDO (or 31-EDO) render places partials at the tuning's cents, proven by the FFT assertion - the directive demonstrably drives the render
with no tuning directive, all existing golden renders are byte-identical
.scl import round-trips a known scale (e.g. Pythagorean) to the correct cents
JI and meantone tables match Barbour's published cents (test)
DSL_SPEC.md marks tuning: as ACTIVE not notational; AGENTS.md documents the supported tuning systems
references: Barbour, Tuning and Temperament (Michigan State 1951; Dover ISBN 978-0-486-43406-3)

items.title: Voice-leading as optimization (minimal-displacement / VL geometry)
items.summary: New audioforge/voice_leading.py computing minimal-displacement bijective voice leading (sum of |semitone motion|) with crossing-free options; add DSL voicing: smooth (new) vs voicing: ornamented (the current heuristic, renamed and kept default); integrate with BL-019's P/L/R.
items.description: DoR: BL-017 (pc-sets) and BL-020 (scales) merged; the objective pinned precisely (minimize summed |delta-semitone| over a bijection; tie-break rule stated) so the result is deterministic. Spec: voice_leading.py minimal-displacement bijection with T-related/inversional options + crossing-free constraints; DSL voicing: smooth (new) vs voicing: ornamented (current L1030 heuristic renamed; unspecified => current default); integrate with BL-019 so P/L/R progressions request smooth voice leading.
items.rationale: The voice-leading logic in dsl.py (~L1030-1106) is a fixed ornament-insertion heuristic (passing tones/suspensions/anticipations + common-tone retention by pc-set intersection). It is NOT minimal-displacement voice leading - it does not compute the voice bijection minimizing total semitone motion. Source: Hook Ch. 10 hexatonic triad graph as continuous VL space (#17); Tymoczko, A Geometry of Music (Oxford 2011, ISBN 978-0-19-533667-2).
acceptance_criteria: for known cases the algorithm returns the textbook minimal voice leading (C major -> G major moves 2 voices by 1-2 semitones, not a leap), verified by test
voicing: ornamented reproduces today's output byte-for-byte (heuristic unchanged, only renamed/defaulted)
voicing: smooth renders and is byte-stable under the golden gate
references: Julian Hook, Exploring Musical Spaces (Oxford 2022, ISBN 978-0-19-024601-3, DOI 10.1093/oso/9780190246013.001.0001) Ch. 10 (#17)
Tymoczko, A Geometry of Music (Oxford 2011, ISBN 978-0-19-533667-2)

items.title: Functional-harmony grammar (roman numerals, cadences, progressions)
items.summary: Add a compile-time expansion layer in dsl.py that, given a key: context, expands Roman-numeral progressions (I vi IV V, ii7 V7 I, secondary dominants, borrowed chords) and cadence templates into the literal chords the engine already renders, reusing BL-020 scales + BL-019 transforms; grammar/GBNF for the numeral surface.
items.description: DoR: BL-019 and BL-020 merged (chromatic transforms + scale/chord construction the expansion relies on); the dialect fixed (which Roman-numeral conventions: figured-bass inversions? applied chords? mode mixture?) to avoid an open-ended grammar. Spec: compile-time expansion in dsl.py given key: (Roman-numeral progression + secondary dominants V/V + borrowed chords => literal chords, reusing BL-020 for diatonic chord construction and BL-019 for functional substitutions); cadence templates (authentic/plagal/half/deceptive) as named sugar; grammar + GBNF productions. Lowest-priority Track-M item - sugar over capabilities the other items provide.
items.rationale: grammar.py expresses harmony only as literal PITCH = note | chord (e.g. C3min7) plus voicing directives - no Roman numerals, function labels (T/S/D), cadence types, or progression templates. A user must spell every chord literally; the DSL cannot say 'a ii-V-I in F' or 'a deceptive cadence'. Grounded in the codebase gap + common-practice pedagogy (Exploring Musical Spaces is deliberately transformational not functional - cited as the complement, not the source; no fabricated citation).
acceptance_criteria: key: F; prog: ii V I expands to the correct literal chords (Gm-C-F) and renders byte-stable
each cadence template produces the textbook chord succession (test)
grammar accepts valid progressions and rejects malformed numerals (test_grammar_token_sync.py extended)
references: Julian Hook, Exploring Musical Spaces (Oxford 2022, ISBN 978-0-19-024601-3, DOI 10.1093/oso/9780190246013.001.0001) (cited as the transformational complement, not the functional source)
